problems: Cliopatria's 'Margraviate of Brandenburg' row holds Bavaria proper in 1326-1351 (77.8-80.5 k km2 = Brandenburg + Bavaria 36.2 k) and its 'Duchy of Bavaria' row holds Brandenburg and Tyrol in 1352-1362 and Brandenburg and the Dutch counties in 1363-1384: margraviate-of-brandenburg (eu-09, other part) must remove Bavaria from 1326-1351 and draw Brandenburg itself for 1352-1384 (Wittelsbach margraves to 1373, then Charles IV).

county-of-holland runs to 1433, past Cliopatria's 1362: the Dutch counties sit inside the Duchy of Bavaria row 1363-1449 and Cliopatria hands them to Burgundy only in 1450. duchy-of-bavaria removes them from its outline; duchy-of-burgundy (eu-10) should take Holland from 1433 and Brabant from 1430.

Cliopatria lumps Luxembourg into Brabant 1415-1421 and into Bavaria 1422-1428, and has its own Luxembourg row only from 1429: duchy-of-luxembourg (eu-09) should cover 1411-1428. Both Brabant and Bavaria dossiers remove it.

Cliopatria's 'House of Wittelsbach' (1260-1332) is, by its outline, Lower Bavaria and probably belongs inside duchy-of-bavaria; it is kept as a separate counterpart here (1340 reunion). Lower Bavaria is nobody's in 1333-1339.

The Brabant row's Wikipedia field 'Landgraviate of Brabant' is the pre-1183 predecessor; the dossier uses 'Duchy of Brabant'. The Bavaria Q47261 and Kingdom of Bavaria Q154195 rows share one colour in colours.json; the dossier ends 1805 with a dissolve event naming kingdom-of-bavaria.
